t: A shaggy, choppy hybrid of the shag and the mullet.
d: The wolf cut has heavy, choppy layers on top and around the crown that thin out toward longer ends, giving volume and a wild, textured shape. It suits wavy and straight hair and works for any gender.
o: A revival of 1970s shag and mullet shapes that took off on TikTok around 2021, popularised partly by Korean hairstylists.
do: Ask for internal layering to remove bulk
dont: Straighten it flat (it loses its shape)
Skip trims: it grows out messy fast
st: Bring reference photos to your stylist
w: Thick or wavy hair, oval or heart faces; works on many lengths.
b: Trims every 8–10 weeks keep it from turning into an unintended mullet.

t: A soft, centre-parted fringe that frames the face.
d: Curtain bangs are longer at the sides and shorter in the middle, parted down the centre so they sweep away like curtains. They soften features and grow out gracefully.
o: Iconic in the late 1960s and 1970s, revived from around 2020 as a low-commitment fringe.
do: Use a round brush to sweep them outward
dont: Let them sit flat and greasy: use dry shampoo
w: Most face shapes, especially long, heart and square faces.
b: Bang trims are often cheap or free between appointments.

t: The chin-length classic, from blunt to French.
d: A bob is cut around the jaw to the shoulders, usually with little layering. Variations include the blunt bob, the French bob (with a fringe, cheekbone to jaw length) and the long bob or 'lob'.
o: Became a symbol of independence in the 1920s and has been reinvented every decade since.
do: Choose blunt ends for fine hair
st: Decide on length: jaw, chin or collarbone
w: Fine to medium hair; oval, heart and square faces (lengths adjusted).
b: A great bob needs frequent trims, so budget for upkeep.

d: A pixie is a short cut, usually shorter at the back and sides with slightly longer pieces on top, often with a side-swept fringe. It shows off bone structure and dries in minutes.
o: Made famous by 1950s and 1960s film and fashion icons and regularly revived on red carpets.
dont: Grow it out without a plan
st: Start with a longer 'bixie' if nervous
w: Oval and heart faces, fine to medium hair, people who want speed.
b: Products cost little, but frequent trims are part of the deal.

t: Layered, feathery and full of movement.
d: The shag uses many choppy layers throughout to create volume at the crown and lightness at the ends. Modern shags are softer and pair beautifully with curtain bangs.
o: A 1970s rock-and-roll staple revived since the late 2010s.
do: Let natural wave do the work
st: Ask for a soft modern shag
w: Wavy or curly hair, medium to thick density.

t: Short face-framing layers that give long hair a bouncy blowout look.
d: The butterfly cut stacks shorter, face-framing layers over long hair so it looks like a short layered cut from the front and long from the back. It creates volume and a 90s blowout effect.
o: Went viral around 2022, inspired by 1990s supermodel blowouts.
dont: Do it on very thin hair without volume products
w: Long, medium-to-thick hair; most face shapes.
b: Velcro rollers are a cheap shortcut to the blowout look.

t: Clean gradient sides that keep any top style sharp.
d: A taper fade gradually shortens the hair at the sideburns and nape, leaving the rest longer. Low tapers are subtle and office-friendly; higher fades are bolder.
o: A barbershop staple with roots in military and Black American barbering traditions, now universal.
k: Works with curls, waves or straight hair
do: Ask for a low taper if you want subtle
Keep the neckline tidy between cuts
Match top length to your face shape
dont: Let it grow more than 3–4 weeks
Use greasy product with a matte look
st: Choose low, mid or high taper
w: Almost everyone; especially good for curly and coily hair.
b: Frequent but quick cuts; learning to tidy the neckline saves money.

t: Short, choppy top with a short fringe: low effort, modern shape.
d: The textured crop keeps hair short with a choppy, textured top pushed forward into a short fringe, usually with faded or tapered sides. It hides a receding hairline well and takes seconds to style.
o: Evolved from the classic French crop and Caesar cut, popular since the 2010s.
do: Pair with a skin or low fade
dont: Let the fringe grow into your eyes
st: Ask for a textured crop with a low fade
w: Straight or wavy hair, thinning hairlines, oval and square faces.
b: One tub of clay lasts months.

t: The ultimate minimal haircut: one clipper guard, zero fuss.
d: A buzz cut is clipped short all over with clippers, sometimes with a slightly longer top (crew cut). It highlights facial features and costs almost nothing to maintain.
o: Long associated with the military; adopted as a fashion statement by many celebrities.
do: Try a bleach or colour for drama
dont: Cut too short if you have scalp scars you dislike
st: Go shorter if you like it
w: Oval, square and angular faces; thinning hair; low-maintenance lovers.
b: A home clipper pays for itself in two months.

t: Your skin, but better: glow, brows and a tint.
d: No-makeup makeup enhances rather than covers: skin tints, concealer only where needed, groomed brows, cream blush and a tinted balm. Skincare is the foundation.
o: A perennial editorial look that peaked with 'skinimalism' and the clean-girl aesthetic in the early 2020s.
do: Prep skin with moisturiser and SPF
st: Swap foundation for a skin tint
Add cream blush high on cheeks
w: Everyone; ideal for daily wear and photos in daylight.
b: Multi-use cream sticks (cheek and lip) cut product costs.

t: Polished, camera-ready makeup in diffused neutrals.
d: Soft glam is full makeup without harsh lines: blended neutral eyeshadow, softly sculpted cheeks, fluffy lashes and a nude or rosy lip. It photographs beautifully and suits events.
o: Popularised by celebrity makeup artists and social media in the late 2010s.
do: Set with a light powder only where needed
st: Blend a taupe shade into the crease
Line and fill lips one shade deeper
w: Events, photos, weddings and nights out.
b: One good neutral palette covers years of soft glam.
